newsitem.title: GERMANY: FDP unanimously approves German tax reform plan.
newsitem.headline: FDP unanimously approves German tax reform plan.

text.p: Germany's Free Democrat Party (FDP) on Thursday gave its unanimous backing to a coalition tax reform plan drawn up under the stewardship of Finance Minister Theo Waigel.
An FDP spokesman said that both the parliamentary party and the party's leadership were in full agreement that the coalition plan should become the basis for tax legislation.

After months of wrangling, Chancellor Helmut Kohl's three-party coalition government agreed on the framework of a two-stage tax plan which would slash income and corporate taxes while scrapping a range of tax breaks.
The plan, to take effect in 1998 and 1999, would reduce the net tax load on Germans by around 30 billion marks. A decision on raising value-added taxes to help finance the reform has been postponed.
